name: Lucius
title: Christian prophet and teacher in Antioch
summary: Lucius of Cyrene was one of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch. He is mentioned alongside Barnabas, Simeon Niger, Manaen, and Saulus as leaders in the early Christian community. He may also be the Lucius whom Paul refers to as his kinsman in Romans.

keyEvents.title: Prophet and teacher in Antioch
keyEvents.description: Lucius of Cyrene is mentioned as one of the five prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch, who served the Lord with fasting and prayer.

keyEvents.title: Sending out of Barnabas and Saul
keyEvents.description: Lucius was present when the Holy Spirit said that Barnabas and Saul should be set apart for the work God had called them to. They laid hands on them and sent them off.

keyEvents.title: Greeting in Romans
keyEvents.description: A person named Lucius is mentioned as Paul's relative who sends greetings to the church in Rome. Many scholars believe this may be the same Lucius from Cyrene.

keyEvents.title: Growth of the Church in Antioch
keyEvents.description: Lucius was likely among the believers from Cyrene who first preached the gospel to Greeks in Antioch, leading many people to faith.

keyEvents.title: Part of the Early Leadership Community
keyEvents.description: As part of the leadership team in Antioch, Lucius helped shape the church that became the first major center for Gentile mission in the early church.
